test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 9 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not conform to real world knowledge, decide which of the given conclusions/possibilities can be true on the basis of the statements.

**Statements : **

1. Some biscuits are cookies.

2. Some cookies are pastries.

3. All pastries are creams.

**Conclusions :**

I. Some pastries are biscuits.

II. Some creams are biscuits.

III. Some creams are cookies.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II are true

solution:
**Given:**

Statements :

1. Some biscuits are cookies.

2. Some cookies are pastries.

3. All pastries are creams.

**Concept used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43300b2984e3c95a3f630f7fa386fcb1544b6321eb3e93e0420e27ad07a4fdbe.png] 

Conclusions :

I. Some pastries are biscuits. **False : **No pastries in contained in biscuits.

II. Some creams are biscuits. **False**** : **No creams is contained in biscuits .

III. Some creams are cookies. **True : **Some part of creams are contained in cookies.

**The correct answer is 'Only conclusion III is true' .**
